tags.name: Convento do Beato

voyage.name: Moda Lisboa
voyage.content: Lisbon Fashion Week.

voyage.name: English Comedy Showcase
voyage.content: Featuring Portuguese and international acts doing their sets in English. A great way to get a deep cultural insight into life in Lisbon through laughter. Usually free entry and donation based.

voyage.name: Peixe em Lisboa
voyage.content: A food festival, with focus on fish dishes.

voyage.name: Dias da Música em Belém
voyage.content: A music festival held in Belém in western Lisbon.

voyage.name: IndieLisboa
voyage.content: An independent film festival. In addition to screenings there is also a large number of lectures and seminars.

voyage.name: Rock in Rio Lisboa
voyage.hours: Late May or early June every other year (every even numbered year)
voyage.content: A major rock music festival, branched from the famous Rock in Rio de Janeiro.

voyage.name: Festas dos Santos
voyage.content: A number of large fiestas celebrating different catholic Saints, with parades during the day and fire work shows by night. The first and largest fiesta celebrates Saint Anthony on 13 June. It is followed by the celebration of Saint John the Baptist on 23 June and Saint Peter on 28 June.

voyage.name: Jazz em Agosto
voyage.content: A annual jazz festival organized by the Gulbenkian Foundation.

voyage.name: MUDE – Museu do Design e da Moda
voyage.hours: Temporarily closed for renovations; planned reopening 2023
voyage.content: The collection has about 1,000 items of furniture and accessories and over 1,200 pieces of haute couture clothing.

voyage.name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha
voyage.alt: Old Church of Our Lady of the Conception
voyage.content: 18th-century Manueline-style church, a national monument.

voyage.name: Palácio Alverca
voyage.alt: Antigo Palácio Pais do Amaral, Antigo Palácio São Luís, Casa do Alentejo
voyage.content: Unassuming from the outside, the interior combines neo-Gothic, neo-Arab, neo-Renaissance, neo-Rococo, Art Nouveau, and baroque elements.

voyage.name: Palácio Foz
voyage.content: A palace constructed in the 18th and 19th centuries. Visits can be arranged in advance via email. Concerts (some of them free) are offered.

voyage.name: Praça do Comércio
voyage.content: This magnificent plaza, facing the river, is the beginning of Lisboa's downtown. It is also known as 'Terreiro do Paço', meaning 'Grounds of the Palace', relating to its function before the Great Earthquake of 1755. The upper floors of the yellow buildings surrounding the square are mainly used as government offices, while the lower floors often contains cafés and restaurants. King Josef I, who ruled during the recon

voyage.name: Praça Dom Pedro IV
voyage.content: One of Lisbon's principal squares. A statue of King Pedro IV stands on a column in the centre. The square, a popular meeting point for local and tourists, is known for its wavy black-and-white stone pavement.

voyage.name: Praça da Figueira
voyage.content: This large square has an equestrian statue of King João I. An important transport hub, the square is surrounded by hotels, cafés, and shops in four-storey buildings dating back to the rebuilding after the 1755 Great Earthquake.

voyage.name: Praça dos Restauradores
voyage.content: This major square lies at the southeast end of Avenida da Liberdade. The Monument to the Restorers, a 30 m obelisk commemorating the 1640 restoration of Portugal as a kingdom separate from Spain, sits in the middle of the square.

voyage.name: Rossio Station
voyage.content: Built in 1890 as the Estação Central (Central Station), it was the main railway hub until 1957. It provides a direct connection to Sintra in about 40 min. The trains access the station through a 2.6-km long tunnel. The main facade is an example of the Neo-Manueline style, a revival of Gothic style in Portugal during the mid-19th century.

voyage.name: Santa Justa Lift
voyage.address: Largo do Carmo - Rua do Ouro
voyage.content: Excellent vertical view of the Baixa streets, next to Igreja do Carmo. The line can be quite long, you may want to consider walking up and riding it down instead.

voyage.name: Teatro Nacional Dona Maria II
voyage.content: The most famous live theatre stage in Lisbon. The Neoclassical and Palladian building was built in the 1840s and has been a national monument since 2003.

voyage.name: Lisboa em Fado
voyage.content: A typical Portuguese Fado concert hall with daily evening shows. Run by a young Fado guitarist from Lisbon. The show lasts about one hour.

voyage.name: Chocolataria Equador
voyage.content: Chocolates, truffles, and barks that are as beautiful as they are delicious. Try the hot chocolate, served elegantly with a chocolate covered cherry.

voyage.name: Leitaria Camponeza
voyage.content: On the location of a historical café (the leitaria), this place focuses on only a short number of dishes (meats, fish and seafood) but makes up for this in quality and portion size. For an atmospheric presentation ask for one of their espetadas. The wines complement the dishes and you can end the meal with a dessert. For someone looking for great value for their buck (no compromises on quality), it's a good place to

voyage.name: Mercado da Praça da Figueira
voyage.content: From the pavement looks like a small convenience shop, on walking in you realize the deception when confronted by the large cavernous meandering interior space, replete with everything expected from a well stocked supermarket. Although there isn't a restaurant as such, the ready to eat items on offer are tasty, fresh, inexpensive and varied. The sandwiches and hamburgers are superb.

voyage.name: Mercado Oriental
voyage.content: A food court serving Asian street food and the only place in Lisbon where you can try Macanese cuisine (at a stall called "Taberna Macau").

voyage.name: Néctar WineBar
voyage.content: A place dedicated to the promotion of Portugal's wine and gastronomic culture, and featuring a daily lunch menu of Portuguese and Mediterranean cuisine. The wine list comprises – in its vast majority – a selection of Portuguese wines which best represent the country. Wine can be bought by the glass, and it is served at the appropriate temperatures and in suitable glasses. Dishes – served in portions for 2 – easily re

voyage.name: Restaurante Bonjardim
voyage.content: Appropriately nicknamed Rei dos Frangos, this is home to the best greasy spit-roasted chicken this side of Louisiana.

voyage.name: Restaurante Gambrinus
voyage.address: Rua das Portas de Santo Antao, 23
voyage.content: A restaurant-bar which is one of the most chic places in the city. Highly recognized in Lisbon as something of an institution, it attracts an eclectic crowd where the appeal is food and a great selection of beers, wines and spirits. Features smoking room, private parking with a doorman.

voyage.name: Bar Trobadores
voyage.content: Medieval bar in downtown with a cozy atmosphere and a diverse range of traditional Portuguese delicacies. National and international beers.

voyage.name: Café Martinho da Arcada
voyage.content: Established in 1782, this is the oldest continuously-operating café in Lisbon and throughout its history has been associated with important politicians, writers, and intellectuals. Writer Fernando Pessoa had a permanent table reservation, as did the late Nobel laureate José Saramago.

voyage.name: Beira Minho
voyage.content: A great location, but with few amenities.

voyage.name: Bom Conforto Casa de Hospedes
voyage.content: Very clean, quiet, and comfortable. Helpful and sweet English-speaking staff.

voyage.name: Hotel Avenida Palace
voyage.content: It's in the emblematic Restauradores Square in a neoclassical building.

voyage.name: Goodnight Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: The interior design looks a bit like IKEA show-room, the staff know where the good places to go out dancing and drinking are and the location works for a budget traveler.

voyage.name: Pensão Norte
voyage.content: B&B style pension with friendly and accommodating staff in a quiet area.

voyage.name: Rossio Hostel
voyage.content: Great location, great staff, great free cooked breakfast, great hostel. The hostel offers dorms and privates. Free internet, TV room, lounge.

voyage.name: Travellers House
voyage.content: Nice hostel with lots of extras. Friendly staff and easy to meet people with their nightly activities. Free WiFi, breakfast, coffee and tea, maps and city advice, lots of guide books to look at and a book exchange for travelers who are tired of reading the same book over and over again.

voyage.name: Yes Hostel
voyage.content: Relaxed and comfortable hostel with an excellent location. One of the largest hostels in Lisbon; opened in July 2009. Comfortable beds in large dorms, key operated lockers, free computer access as well as WiFi in every room, free breakfast, complimentary coffee and tea, 24 hour bar, access to their professional kitchen. Very friendly and accommodating staff. 3-course Portuguese dinners for €8 by their in-house chef.

voyage.name: Igreja do Carmo
voyage.hours: Oct-May: Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00; Jun-Sep: Mon-Sat 10:00-19:00; closed Sun, 1 Jan, 1 May, 25 Dec
voyage.content: The hilltop church of the former convent of Carmo is a towering memorial of the 1755 earthquake, which made the roof of the church collapse, but the Gothic arches of the nave survived. The church was preserved that way and now serves as the Museu Arqueológico in the extant parts of the building. The museum houses a hodgepodge of archaeological artifacts from around Portugal and the world including mummies from South

voyage.name: Jardim de São Pedro de Alcântara
voyage.content: Excellent panorama from the lovely terrace/garden on top of Elevador da Glória and northern corner of Bairro Alto.

voyage.name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
voyage.content: Portugal's impressive national art collection, including 14-19th century European painting, artefacts of Portuguese contact with the East and Africa and a collection of ecclesiastical treasures. Highlights include Dürer's St Jerome, Hieronymus Bosch's Temptations of St Antony, Nuno Gonçalves' Adoration of St Vincent, and 16th century Japanese paintings of Portuguese traders.

voyage.name: Museu da Marioneta
voyage.price: Admission 5 EUR, ages 13–25 2.50 EUR, 65+ or disabled 4.30 EUR, kids under 13 free; shows 7.50 EUR, kids, seniors 65+, and students under 25 5 EUR
voyage.address: Convento das Bernardas, Rua da Esperança 146
voyage.content: The museum covers the history of puppetry around the world, with an emphasis on Portugal. Various types of puppets are on display.

voyage.name: Basílica da Estrela
voyage.content: This Neoclassical and Baroque basilica, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, was built in the late 1700s by Queen Maria I in fulfilment of a vow. The Queen is entombed in the right transept. Among the artworks is a nativity scene made up of over 500 cork and terracotta figures by Joaquim Machado de Castro.

voyage.name: Jardim da Estrela
voyage.content: A English-style garden with Romantic inspiration. You can find many plant and bird species here.

voyage.name: Palácio de São Bento
voyage.content: Built in 1598, the palace has served as the home of Portugal's parliament since 1834. The adjoining São Bento Mansion serves as the prime minister's residence.

voyage.name: Cemitério dos Prazeres
voyage.content: This large cemetery is packed with majestic gravestones and mausoleums, separated by wide, pedestrian, tree-lined "streets". Many graves are marked with icons telling something about the person's role in historical Lisbon. A beautiful respite from the busy city.

voyage.name: Fundação Arpad Szenes / Vieira da Silva
voyage.content: This museum is installed in the restored 18th-century former Royal Silk Factory. Its permanent collection covers a wide time period of the works of 20th-century painters Arpad Szenes and Maria Helena Vieira da Silva, and regularly hosts exhibits by their contemporaries.

voyage.name: Aqueduto das Aguas Livres
voyage.content: This is a historic aqueduct in the city of Lisbon, Portugal. It is one of the most remarkable examples of 18th-century Portuguese engineering, including the largest stone arch in the world. The main course of the aqueduct covers 18 km, but the whole network of canals extends through nearly 58 km. The Mãe d'Água (Mother of the Water) reservoir of the Amoreiras, the largest of the water reservoirs, was finished in 1834

voyage.name: Espaço Novo Banco
voyage.content: Multifunctional space dedicated to contemporary art, especially photography.

voyage.name: Lisbon Botanical Gardens
voyage.price: Entrance €5 adults, discounts for kids, seniors and students
voyage.content: A hidden gem. It was created several hundred years ago, by a King of Portugal at the time of the Discoveries. The story goes that this King wanted one of every type of plant in the world, and although that's unlikely, there is a huge collection dating back by three or four centuries which is worth checking out. And there's something quite eerie about seeing plants or huge trees from completely different climates grow

voyage.name: Teatro Maria Vitória
voyage.content: Presenting teatro de revista, Portuguese-style comedy revues. The theatre opened in 1922 and was restored in 1990 following a 1986 fire.

voyage.name: Armazéns do Chiado
voyage.content: This upscale and trendy shopping centre was developed inside Lisbon's historic grand department store which burnt down in 1988. The food court on the top floor has a terrace with a brilliant view over Baixa and Chiado.

voyage.name: Centro Comercial Amoreiras
voyage.content: The city's oldest mall in eye-catching post-modern towers housing international chains.

voyage.name: Mercado de Campo de Ourique
voyage.content: An indoor market selling wide selection of fruits, vegetables, meats, fish, and jewelry. A perfect break while Tram 28 turns around, it's calmer and less crowded than other markets listed.

voyage.name: A Vida Portuguesa
voyage.content: Vintage and nostalgic products and brands.

voyage.name: Livraria Bertrand
voyage.content: Founded in 1732, it is the oldest operating bookstore in the world. If you want they can stamp the books you buy, certifying that they were bought there. While most books are in Portuguese there is a full shelf of English language literature, including many notable Portuguese titles translated to English. There's a small coffee-shop/bar area at the back of the shop with very helpful staff.

voyage.name: Caza das Vellas Loreto
voyage.content: A shop that has been selling beautiful homemade candles since 1789.

voyage.name: Restaurante Tascardoso
voyage.content: Standing-room only, this place serves simple and affordable Portuguese dishes, including grilled sardines. Toilets available.

voyage.name: Taberna Minhota
voyage.address: R. de São Pedro de Alcântara 13
voyage.content: A tapas restaurant

voyage.name: A Cabana da Estrela
voyage.address: R. da Bela Vista à Lapa 20

voyage.name: Time Out Market
voyage.content: The late 19th-century market was closed in 2000, and in 2014 the publisher Time Out Portugal transformed the space into a gourmet food court with 40 kiosks, including restaurants, bars, and shops. A number of Lisbon's top chefs have stands here, making this an ideal place to sample some of their food for lower prices than at their established restaurants.

voyage.name: Rosa da Rua Restaurante
voyage.content: A traditional restaurant offering an interesting mix of Portuguese, Indian, and Cape Verdean flavours. The lunch-time buffet offers excellent value for money and great quality food. Staff are patient with English speakers.

voyage.name: Faca & Garfo
voyage.content: A cozy and affordable restaurant which offers tasty grilled Portuguese specialities of meat and fish.

voyage.name: Bengal Tandoori
voyage.content: Cuisine of East Bengal, India, using a tandoor oven.

voyage.name: Cervejaria da Trindade
voyage.content: This excellent restaurant-brewery in a former monastery has several kinds of Sagres beer and Guinness. The appetizer that is charged for each item that is consumed separately. Nice codfish plates.

voyage.name: Os Tibetanos
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant affiliated with a Buddhist center. Vegan friendly. Juice bar.

voyage.name: Tamarind
voyage.content: Small Indian restaurant. Reservations can be made online.

voyage.name: Restaurante Brasuca
voyage.content: Great Brazilian food served by friendly staff.

voyage.name: Restaurante Calcutá 2
voyage.content: The second of two restaurants operated by the same owners. Decent Indian food, but far from the best. The location is great though for starting a night out on the town. Ask for the shoot drinks!

voyage.name: Restaurante Lisboa À Noite
voyage.content: A restaurant with a variety of traditional Portuguese dishes very appreciated by the tourists. Friendly environment, great service. Make sure you try the appetizers.

voyage.name: Restaurante Sacramento do Chiado
voyage.content: A popular locals' place in palace stables from the 18th-century . The atmosphere and the food are excellent. Service is very good and the recommendations by the staff are outstanding. The writing on the menu is very small and difficult to read in the subdued lighting.

voyage.name: Restaurante Sinal Vermelho
voyage.content: Good traditional Portuguese at reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Restaurante Terra
voyage.content: Probably the best vegetarian restaurant in Lisbon and also the nicest in terms of ambience and service. They have a menu in English and will help with vegan choices or people with other dietary restrictions. Reservations are recommended, especially on weekends but you will always be served even if you arrive with the place full and have to wait for a while. Weather permitting try to get a table outside, which means a

voyage.name: Come Prima
voyage.content: Traditional Italian fresh pasta dishes, various starters, risottos, meats and wood-oven pizzas are produced from a wide selection of prime quality fresh ingredients. Extensive wine list procured from both national and Italian producers and a delightful choice of desserts carefully picked from the Italian classics.

voyage.name: Café Buenos Aires
voyage.content: A good and selected combination of cheap and mid range dishes. The owners are very friendly and speak English, as well as Portuguese. It is a good restaurant if you want to eat South American grilled meat.

voyage.name: Belcanto
voyage.content: Contemporary Portuguese cuisine with two Michelin stars.

voyage.name: Alma
voyage.content: Two-Michelin-star fine dining by chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, blending traditional Portuguese cuisine with Asian influences. Choose from two tasting menus or order à la carte.

voyage.name: Loco Restaurante
voyage.content: Michelin-starred restaurant offering two tasting menus using local ingredients by chef Alexandre Silva, who won the first series of Top Chef de Portugal.

voyage.name: 100 Maneiras
voyage.content: Michelin-starred restaurant by Bosnian chef Ljubomir Stanisic, who blends influences from his homeland, his adopted country, and elsewhere around the globe.

voyage.name: Epur
voyage.address: Largo da Academia Nacional de Belas Artes 14
voyage.content: Michelin-starred restaurant by French chef Vincent Farges, who prepares an edgy surprise menu centred on visual elegance and purity of flavours.

voyage.name: Café A Brasileira
voyage.price: Prices are in three levels, depending on where you choose to drink: cheapest standing at the counter, and most expensive sitting outside on the terrace
voyage.content: One of Lisbon's remaining classic cafés, with a restaurant in the basement; despite renovation, not much has changed since the 1920s. The café was Fernando Pessoa's favourite place, and a statue of the poet/philosopher stands outside the main entrance on the terrace.

voyage.name: Manteigaria - Fábrica de Pastéis de Nata
voyage.content: A bakery serving some of the best pastéis de nata in town, arguably the best in Lisbon. You can even watch them make the pasteis de nata. Standing room only.

voyage.name: Chafariz do Vinho
voyage.content: Perfect place to linger over a glass of wine at this wine bar that is under the arches of the city's former acquaducts. With a great selection of appetizers that are matched perfectly with the wine, it's a pleasant way to spend an evening.

voyage.name: Garrafeira Alfaia
voyage.content: Nice wine bar with an impressive selection of good wines and appetizers. Good place to spend the late afternoon, before going out to dinner.

voyage.name: Tivoli Hotel Sky Bar
voyage.content: The superbly located rooftop bar of Tivoli Hotel is a small secret. On warm evenings one of the best places to have an overpriced late drink. Youngish music late night.

voyage.name: Fado In Chiado
voyage.content: Fado In Chiado - Daily show (except on Sundays) at 19:00, with a duration of 50 minutes. Voices that sing the Fado to the sound of Portuguese guitar.

voyage.name: Tasca do Chico
voyage.content: A cramped but authentic Fado bar.

voyage.name: Lisbon Old Town Hostel
voyage.content: A hostel, opened in 2007, catering to the young hip crowd with event listings on their website, free computer and internet access in the lobby and WiFi throughout the hostel.

voyage.name: Poets Hostel
voyage.content: The building is next the Chiado exit of the Baixa-Chiado metro station. Very helpful staff, clean rooms, dinners and activities are organized by the hostel. Big common room with TV and free internet. Dorms and privates available.

voyage.name: InSuites Chiado Apartments I
voyage.content: In the center of the Chiado, these apartments have 1 and 2 bedrooms.

voyage.name: InSuites Chiado Apartments II
voyage.content: Luxury apartments in the historical Chiado, Lisbon center, with 3 bedrooms.

voyage.name: Bed&Breakfast Lisboa
voyage.content: Good rooms in a very central bed-and-breakfast with views all over Lisbon and the river.

voyage.name: Camões
voyage.content: Basic, clean and affordable.

voyage.name: Oasis Backpackers' Mansion
voyage.content: Backpackers rave about this hotel, often noting the friendly staff, large clean rooms, fun atmosphere and great dinners. It is a great place for a budget traveler to meet up with other travelers and feel safe when they go to bed at night - if they go to bed.

voyage.name: Pensão Alegria
voyage.content: Small cosy pension on a beautiful small square.

voyage.name: Hotel Portuense
voyage.address: Rua das Portas de Santo Antão 149-157

voyage.name: Lisboa Central Hostel
voyage.content: A fun, fresh and friendly place to stay in the heart of city in Marques de Pombal and Avenida da Liberdade. This international hostel provides a good base for sight-seeing by day and partying by night. All of Lisbon’s major night spots are easily accessible on foot.

voyage.name: Residencial Vila Nova
voyage.content: Two-star, 30-room, modern guest house close to Marques de Pombal station.

voyage.name: Hotel Borges Chiado
voyage.content: Three-star, 100-room hotel. Spacious rooms with satellite TV. Very central, but somewhat expensive for the service.

voyage.name: NH Collection Lisboa Liberdade
voyage.content: Nice four-star, 108-room hotel in the center of the city. Seasonal rooftop pool, lawned terrace, bar, free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express Lisbon - Av. Liberdade
voyage.content: Three-star, 108-room modern hotel with compact but efficient rooms, with kettle and mini-fridge. Near Avenida da Liberdade and the view from Parque Eduardo VII, and within walking distance of the old town. Nearby shops and restaurants are less crowded with tourists than those further south. Two metro lines give access to most areas of the city, and frequent bus 727 runs directly to the Belém museum district. Price in

voyage.name: Olissippo Lapa Palace
voyage.content: Five-star, 109-room hotel, property of Orient-Express Hotels, Trains & Cruises. A luxury palace hotel in one of Lisbon's seven hills, with gardens and pools, heated all year long. Member of the Leading Hotels of the World. With one of the best spas in Lisbon, gourmet food (its restaurant is considered by the Zagat Guide as one of the best in Lisbon) and one of the best concierge services in the country.

voyage.name: Eurostars das Letras
voyage.content: Five-star, 107-room modern hotel in the central Rato district. The hotel offers free wireless internet for guests along with two laptops with internet access.

voyage.name: Sofitel Lisbon Liberdade
voyage.content: Five-star, 163-room hotel. Perhaps not particularly outstanding in standards or appointments among other Sofitels in Europe (meaning though that the standards are very high), the Lisbon Sofitel boasts a very central location on the Avenida da Liberdade, smack right at the entrance to the namesake metro station.

voyage.name: Tivoli Avenida Liberdade Lisboa
voyage.content: The five-star, 285-room flagship of the Portuguese Tivoli hotel chain is most known for its rooftop terrace bar with splendid views.

voyage.name: Altis Grand Hotel
voyage.content: Five-star, 295 room hotel with swimming pool, spa, gym, business centre, conference facilities, bar, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Fontecruz Lisboa
voyage.content: Striking postmodern architecture and interior appointments are on the menu throughout this Marriott's luxury, five-star, 72-room boutique hotel.

voyage.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
voyage.content: Good viewpoint in Alfama uphill from the cathedral along tram route. Lovely view over rooftops and river.

voyage.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
voyage.content: The highest viewpoint in Lisbon, at the top of the Graça hill, spread out in front of the small Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monte (founded in 1147, remodelled in the 20th century). To the south you look down over the Castelo de São Jorge, the Mouraria and the Baixa to the Tagus estuary; to the west, from Bairro Alto out to the Monsanto forest; to the north, down the Avenida Almirante Reis valley. It sits a little furt

voyage.name: Castelo de São Jorge
voyage.price: 15 EUR, ages 13–25 7.5 EUR, disabled or seniors 65+ 7.50 EUR, children under 12 free; guided tour 5 EUR
voyage.content: Humans settled on this hill as early as the 8th century BCE, and the first fortifications date from the 1st century BCE. Before the Portuguese conquest in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon, the site was successively occupied by the Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors. Sights within the castle include the permanent exhibition of archaeological artefacts with an emphasis on the 11th- and 12th-century Moors, ruins of t

voyage.name: Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
voyage.alt: Monastery of St. Vincent Outside the Walls
voyage.content: Started in 1582, this Mannerist monastery wasn't completed until 1629, following the reconstruction of a 1147 church under royal decree. The church houses the Pantheon of the House of Braganza, where many monarchs, consorts, and their offspring are entombed.

voyage.name: Lisbon Cathedral
voyage.alt: Sé de Lisboa, Igreja de Santa Maria Maior
voyage.price: 5 EUR, children 7–12 2.50 EUR, children 6 & under free
voyage.content: Built in 1147, the cathedral has survived various earthquakes and has undergone restoration, renovation, and modification over the years. Its elements include Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. It has been a national monument since 1910.

voyage.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
voyage.price: 5 EUR, seniors 65+/students/youth card 2.50 EUR, disabled & children 12 and under free
voyage.content: One of the most important national museums, dedicated to Portuguese azulejo tiles since the late 1400s. It's in the former Madre de Deus Convent, founded in 1509 by Queen Leonor.

voyage.name: Museu Militar de Lisboa
voyage.content: Housed in a 16th-century foundry, this museum holds its testaments to Portuguese military history, and contains many artifacts, including a sword used by Vasco da Gama.

voyage.name: Museu de Sociedade de Geografia
voyage.alt: Museu Etnográfico da Sociedade de Geografia de Lisboa
voyage.price: 5 EUR, seniors 65+ 2 EUR, students & youths 2.50 EUR, families of 4 or more 4 EUR each, disabled & children 12 and under free
voyage.address: Rua das Portas de Santo Antão 100
voyage.content: Exhibits of ethnography from Portugal's former colonies.

voyage.name: Museu do Teatro Romano
voyage.address: Rua de São Mamede, nº 3 A
voyage.content: Along the way from downtown to Saint George's Castle.

voyage.name: Panteão Nacional
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00, platform 10:00-18:00 (closed Mondays, shorter hours in winter)
voyage.content: This is one of the most striking buildings in Lisbon. Its tall dome and white facade makes it a real landmark in Alfama/Eastern Lisbon. Excellent views from the rooftop terrace. Construction began in 1681, then halted until the dome was added in 1966 and then converted to the National Pantheon. Amália Rodrigues, queen of fado, is buried here, and fresh roses can be seen on the tomb. The church also has wide viewing p

voyage.name: Coliseu dos Recreios
voyage.address: Rua das Portas de Santo Antão 96
voyage.content: Large multi-purpose auditorium for musical performances.

voyage.name: Feira da Ladra
voyage.content: A lively outdoor market offering new and used products. Markets of this type have pleased bargain hunters since the 12th century in Lisbon and the Feira da Ladra name has been around since the 17th century.

voyage.name: Restaurante Santa Rita
voyage.content: Authentic, cheap Portuguese dishes in a very busy, shared-table restaurant.

voyage.name: Velha Gaiteira
voyage.content: A charming spot with a welcoming host. A delicious prix fixe meal was €12.50.

voyage.name: Chapitô à Mesa
voyage.content: Great views are the main feature if you reserve terrace seat in advance. Good atmosphere; international-menu food is tasty but nothing special.

voyage.name: Farol de Santa Luzia
voyage.content: Great place to have typical Portuguese food before climbing to Castelo S. Jorge.

voyage.name: Malmequer Bemmequer
voyage.content: Friendly and inexpensive; long menu of traditional Portuguese dishes.

voyage.name: Portuel Kosher Store
voyage.content: Lisbon's source for kosher groceries.

voyage.name: Zambeze
voyage.content: A Mozambique restaurant on a "miradouro", viewing spot, offering a great view of the river, the Baixa area, and beyond. An elevator can bring you up and down the deep slopes, making it easily reachable from the nearby Baixa area.

voyage.name: Lux Fragil
voyage.address: Av. Infante D. Henrique, Armazém A
voyage.content: It's in a former warehouse and part owned by American actor John Malkovich.

voyage.name: Pois Café
voyage.content: It's a place to relax, read a book, drink a coffee and plan your way around Lisbon. Also offers toasts, pastas, quiches and salads; features late breakfasts.

voyage.name: Portas do Sol
voyage.content: A cafe and bar on a "Miradouro", viewing spot, and thus offer a spectacular view over the Alfama rooftops down to the river.

voyage.name: Alfama Patio Apartments
voyage.content: Two-star out-of-the-way lodging (but it's directly on the Tram line 28). Full amenities from fast Wi-Fi to free crepe breakfast only compliment the fun staff, who sometimes even go out with you at night.

voyage.name: Ibis Lisboa Centro Saldanha Hotel
voyage.content: Two-star, 116-room hotel. Travelers give this Ibis so-so reviews noting on the plus side the location only 5 min walk to the metro, and a good breakfast and on the minus side small rooms.

voyage.name: Johnies Place Hostel
voyage.content: Cosy hostel. No extra costs for Wi-Fi, printing, breakfast (for private rooms).

voyage.name: Lisbon Story Guesthouse
voyage.content: Cozy three-star, 11-room guesthouse with welcoming common areas and well-decorated small rooms at a budget price.

voyage.name: The One Palácio da Anunciada
voyage.address: Rua das Portas de Santo Antão 112-134
voyage.content: Five-star, 83-room hotel in a 16th-century palace with contemporary guest rooms. The old noble rooms now serve as dining areas. Guests can enjoy of gardens, two swimming pools, spa, fitness centre, meeting rooms, business centre, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Torel Palace Lisbon
voyage.content: The four-star, 31-room Torel Palace is a boutique hotel on top of Sant'ana hill. From the carefully renovated two palaces and the outside gardens, terraces and the pool, visitors enjoy a stunning view over the city. Named after Portuguese Queens and Kings, each of the rooms is unique and offers an elegant home. Owned by a Portuguese and two Austrians. Offers breakfast all day long.

voyage.name: Hotel Travel Park Lisboa
voyage.content: Three-star, 61-room hotel that sits in the heart of Av. Almirante Reis. Just five minutes away from Lisbon International Airport and with underground station at doorstep.

voyage.name: Ajuda Botanical Gardens
voyage.content: The botanical garden of Ajuda is one of the oldest gardens in Europe and is considered the first in Portugal. After the earthquake that occurred in 1755, the homeless Portuguese royal family decided to build a new royal residence at Ajuda but also gardens around it. This 10-acre garden was laid out in from 1858-1873.

voyage.name: Centro Cultural de Belém
voyage.content: CCB is a complex of artistic and cultural venues. It has spaces for meetings and conferences, performing arts (film, opera, ballet, theatre, and music), and art exhibits (art, architecture, design, and photography).

voyage.name: Monument to the Discoveries
voyage.content: Climbing the monument gives you a spectacular view of Belém.

voyage.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
voyage.price: €18 (adults), €9 (seniors/students/youth card), free (children under 12); free admission to the church and on first Sun of the month. Note that tickets are sold from the neighbouring archeological museum, not at the monastery entrance
voyage.hours: Oct-May: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:30; May-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:30; last entry 30 min before closing; closed 1 Jan, Easter, 1 May, 13 Jun, and 25 Dec
voyage.content: A , the monastery was built in the 16th century and is an outstanding example of the Portuguese late Gothic Manueline style.

voyage.name: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
voyage.alt: MAAT – Museu de Arte, Arquitetura e Tecnologia
voyage.price: Adults 9 EUR, kids 12+/students/seniors 65+ 6 EUR, kids under 12 free,15 Jul–31 Aug: 20% discount off all tickets (admission includes Tejo Power Station)
voyage.hours: Wed–Mon 11:00–19:00 (Jun–Sep: Fri Sat until 22:00), closed Tue
voyage.content: This museum of contemporary art is housed in a riverside building of contemporary design.

voyage.name: Museu Colecção Berardo
voyage.content: The permanent collection of the museum consists of the Berardo Collection, which is made up of modern and contemporary art, with major art movements like abstract expressionism, Abstraction-Création, action painting, body Art, constructivism, cubism, De Stijl, digital art, experimental art, geometric abstraction, kinetic art, minimal art, neo-expressionism, neo-plasticism, neo-Realism, op art, photography, photoreali

voyage.name: Museu da Marinha
voyage.price: Adults 7.00 EUR, seniors 65+ & youths 4–12 3.50 EUR, kids 0–3 free, family (2 adults & 2 youths) 18.00 EUR
voyage.content: One of the most important in Europe, evoking Portugal's domination of the seas. Its colossal 17,000 items are installed in the west wing of Jerónimos Monastery, and include model ships from the Age of Discovery onward. The oldest exhibit is a wooden figure representing the Archangel Raphael that accompanied Vasco da Gama on his voyage to India.

voyage.name: Museu Nacional dos Coches
voyage.content: Housed in the former riding school of the palace, don't miss the world's largest collection of horse-drawn coaches and other royal vehicles. One of Lisbon's many unusual museums. In the "Museum street", Belem.

voyage.name: Planetário Calouste Gulbenkian
voyage.price: Adults 5 EUR, seniors 65+ & kids 4-12 2.50 EUR, kids 0-3 free, family (2 adults & 2 youths) 12 EUR
voyage.hours: Temporarily closed for renovations; planned reopening Oct 2021
voyage.content: The planetarium has 32 star projectors, capable of presenting more than 9,000 stars. It holds a chunk of moon rock given by U.S. President Richard Nixon.

voyage.name: Ponte 25 de Abril
voyage.content: This sister bridge of the San Francisco – Oakland Bay Bridge was designed by the same architect in 1966 to connect Lisbon with the Setubal peninsula across the Tagus (Tejo) River. Formerly known as the Salazar Bridge, it was renamed after the Carnation Revolution which, on 25 April 1974, ended the dictatorship.

voyage.name: Statue to Afonso de Albuquerque
voyage.content: In front of the former Royal Palace of Belém, now the Presidential Palace, there is a massive statue looking out to sea, representing Afonso de Albuquerque, second ruler of Portuguese India in the early 16th century.

voyage.name: Tejo Power Station
voyage.alt: Central Tejo, f/k/a Museu da Electricidade, Electricity Museum
voyage.price: Admission included in the price of the Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
voyage.content: This disused power station is now a museum dedicated to the science, industry, and history of electricity production in Portugal.

voyage.name: Torre de Belém
voyage.price: €6 (adults), €3 (seniors/students/youth card), free (children under 12); free admission on first Sun of the month. Combined ticket with Mosteiro dos Jerónimos €12, combined ticket with Mosteiro dos Jerónimos and Museu Nacional de Arqueologia €16, combined ticket with 5 other sites €25 (see website for details)
voyage.hours: Oct-May: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:30; May-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:30; last entry 30 min before closing; closed 1 Jan, Easter, 1 May, 13 Jun, and 25 Dec
voyage.content: A , the iconic fortified tower was built in the early 16th century in the late Gothic Manueline style as a fortress. It was said to be the last thing Portuguese explorers saw when departing, and the first thing they saw upon return. It was later used as a prison for political prisoners, and is today one of the most recognized symbols of Lisbon and Portugal.

voyage.name: Museu da Carris
voyage.content: Transport museum with various old trams and buses on display.

voyage.name: Quake - Lisbon Earthquake Centre
voyage.alt: Quake - Centro do Terramoto de Lisboa
voyage.content: A fully interactive museum on the Lisbon Earthquake of 1755.

voyage.name: Selva Comedy Cafe: Life in Lisboa - A cultural comedy show
voyage.content: This comedy show is 100% in English and features well known comedians from the local and international scene in Lisbon. The comedians have experienced dating disasters, rental nightmares, cultural quirks, and they will tell it all. It's a night full of hilarity and good times. A great way to gain a cultural insight into what it's like being a Lisboeta.

voyage.name: Eneko Lisboa
voyage.content: Michelin-starred restaurant by Spanish Basque chef Eneko Atxa. Attached to a more laid-back space called "Basque".

voyage.name: Feitoria
voyage.content: Michelin-starred seafood restaurant by the docks.

voyage.name: A Marítima do Restelo
voyage.content: Seafood restaurant by the water.

voyage.name: Prova - Enoteca
voyage.content: Modern, urban wine bar serving seafood and sausage & cheese platters in a convivial atmosphere.

voyage.name: Taberna dos Ferreiros
voyage.content: A fresh take on Mediterranean cuisine.

voyage.name: Pastéis de Belém
voyage.content: The most famous of pastelarias, and justly so. They are served right out of the oven there, with the side of confectioner's sugar and cinnamon. As you navigate through the tile-covered labyrinthine passages of the expansive shop, stop to look at the workers behind glass panels turning the endless stream of these delicacies, just baked, each in its own little ramekin, over onto the waiting trays. These are absolutely

voyage.name: Altis Belem Hotel & Spa
voyage.content: Five-star, 50-room hotel overlooking the Tagus with pool, spa, gym, bar, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Hotel Jerónimos 8
voyage.content: Four-star, 65-room hotel with bar, sauna, free breakfast, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Nau Palácio do Governador
voyage.content: Five-star, 60 room hotel with spa, gym, two swimming pools, business centre, free breakfast, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Pestana Palace Lisboa
voyage.content: Five-star, 192-room hotel in an old palace, with a wonderful garden and luxury spa.

voyage.name: Vila Galé Ópera
voyage.content: Four-star, 259-room hotel next to the Tagus River. Adjoins Lisbon’s Congress Centre and the lively nightlife of Lisbon’s Docas area.

voyage.name: Feira Internacional de Lisboa
voyage.content: This venue, the size of 11 football pitches, hosts trade shows and similar exhibitions.

voyage.name: Jardim Garcia de Orta
voyage.content: A pleasant riverside garden with sculptures and other artworks.

voyage.name: Lisbon Oceanarium
voyage.price: Adults 19 EUR, seniors 65+ 13 EUR, children 4–12 10 EUR, children 0–3 free, family (2 adults + 2 children up to age 12) 47 EUR, extra child 6 EUR
voyage.content: One of the world's largest aquariums. Built by American architect Peter Chermayeff, it hosts thousands of marine species of the oceans, such as sea otters, penguins, and sharks. The main tank is huge, representing the Atlantic environment, with hundreds of small fishes, sharks, barracuda, snappers, and a huge sunfish. Ideal for children.

voyage.name: Pavilhão do Conhecimento - Centro Ciência Viva
voyage.alt: Pavilion of Knowledge - Living Science Centre
voyage.price: Adults 10 EUR, seniors 65+ 7 EUR, youths 12–17 8 EUR, children 3–11 7 EUR, children 2 & under free, family (2 adults + children under 17) 25 EUR
voyage.content: Ciência Viva is an interactive science and technology museum that aims to make science accessible to all, stimulating experimentation and exploration of the physical world.

voyage.name: Ponte Vasco da Gama
voyage.content: It is the longest bridge in Europe (including viaducts), and ninth longest in the world, with a total length of 17.2 km, including 0.829 km for the main bridge, 11.5 km in viaducts, and 4.8 km in dedicated access roads.

voyage.name: Altice Arena
voyage.alt: formerly MEO Arena, originally Pavilhão Atlântico
voyage.content: This 20,000-seat arena hosts touring rock bands and Brazilian musicians.

voyage.name: Casino Lisboa
voyage.content: Among the gambling opportunities here are slot machines, poker, roulette, black jack, and baccarat. They have two restaurants, four bars, two entertainment venues, and an art gallery.

voyage.name: Teleférico do Parque das Nações
voyage.price: Adults 6.50 EUR one-way, 8 EUR round-trip; kids 4–12 4.50 EUR one-way, 5.50 EUR round-trip; kids 0–3 free
voyage.content: An aerial tramway built for Expo '98. It operates between the Oceanarium and the Vasco da Gama Tower and offers excellent views of the fairgrounds, the river, the bridge, and beyond.

voyage.name: Centro Vasco da Gama
voyage.content: A large shopping mall in the Parque Expo, featuring many international brands and a food court. There are 170 stores, including 33 restaurants, a health club, a hypermarket, and a 6-screen cinema.

voyage.name: A Avó Tinha
voyage.content: A modern take on traditional Portuguese dishes.

voyage.name: D'Bacalhau
voyage.content: Specializing in cod, they also serve steaks and other fish. It's along the river with nice views from the upstairs dining room.

voyage.name: Fifty Seconds
voyage.content: Michelin-starred restaurant by Spanish chef Martín Berasategui, in the Myriad Sana Hotel 120 m up the Vasco da Gama Tower, offering spectacular views.

voyage.name: Oásis Vegetariano
voyage.content: Vegetarian and vegan dishes.

voyage.name: Páteo Restaurante
voyage.address: Edifício Adamastor, Avenida Dom João II 11B
voyage.content: Traditional Portuguese cuisine.

voyage.name: HI Parque das Nações Youth Hostel
voyage.content: 18-room youth hostel with free breakfast and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Ibis Lisboa Parque das Nações Hotel
voyage.content: Three-star, 112-room hotel with bar, gym, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Myriad
voyage.content: Five-star, 186-room hotel at the Vasco da Gama Tower offering panoramic river views. Amenities include indoor pool, spa, gym, restaurant, and bar.

voyage.name: Olissippo Oriente
voyage.content: Four-star, 182-room hotel with bar, conference facilities, business centre, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Tivoli Oriente Lisboa Hotel
voyage.content: Four-star, 279-room hotel with swimming pool, gym, restaurant, bar, and conference facilities.

voyage.name: Meliá Lisboa Oriente
voyage.content: Four-star, 207-room hotel with restaurant, bar, conference facilities, concierge, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
voyage.content: One of the best museums in Lisbon. Created from the personal collection of the art and artifact collector Calouste Gulbenkian. The collection include Egyptian artefacts; Islamic and oriental art; paintings by masters such as Rembrandt, Manet, Monet, Renoir, and Cassat; and a large collection of objects made by the Art Nouveau jeweler René Lalique. Gulbenkian was an Armenian born in the Ottoman Empire who, through his

voyage.name: Centro de Arte Moderna
voyage.hours: Daily 10:00 – 18:00, closed on Tuesdays, 10:00 – 21:00 on Saturdays
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to art since the 1950s, focusing on Portuguese artists and including other nationalities, notably British and Armenian. Part of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation.

voyage.name: Jardim Zoológico
voyage.content: A zoo that is fairly pricey, but has a variety of exotic animals featuring sea-lions and dolphins.

voyage.name: Parque Eduardo VII
voyage.content: Formal park with expansive views down toward the city and water from Miradouro Parque Eduardo VII. Home to the wonderful Estufa Fria greenhouse gardens.

voyage.name: Praça Marquês de Pombal
voyage.content: Essentially a large roundabout with a sizeable statue of a former Portuguese prime minister in the middle.

voyage.name: Gulbenkian Music
voyage.content: The Gulbenkian Foundation has its own symphony orchestra and ballet group. There are also two stages operated by the foundation. One major auditorium inside the main building, and an outdoors stage in the nearby Gulbenkian Gardens.

voyage.name: Monsanto Forest Park
voyage.content: A municipal protected forest, the largest green patch in the city, covering almost 10 km². It offers a well-diversified, tree-covered area. 50 ha is set aside as the Ecological Park, which runs an interpretation centre, with space for permanent and occasional exhibitions, and a Centre of Multimedia Resources.

voyage.name: Centro Colombo
voyage.content: One of the largest malls in Europe, this shopping and leisure complex also houses dozens of restaurants, a bowling alley, health club and a multiplex cinema.

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés
voyage.content: The Spanish department store chain invaded Lisbon, armed with cinema and supermarket. It can be a bit pricey but with good quality items.

voyage.name: O Cubo
voyage.address: Rua Dom Francisco Manuel de Melo 16B
voyage.content: A place for a family meal or a business lunch.

voyage.name: Eleven
voyage.content: Michelin-starred restaurant in Jardim Amália Rodrigues with views of Parque Eduardo VII.

voyage.name: Fábrica Imperial
voyage.content: They say they serve grandma's cooking with the love of a grandchild.

voyage.name: Il Gattopardo
voyage.content: An elegant restaurant serving fashionable gourmet Italian.

voyage.name: America Diamonds Hotel
voyage.content: Three-star, 66-room hotel, totally reconstructed in 2006 in a historical building, keeping only its original façade, contrasting with its modern interior. Amenities include bar, restaurant, room service, free breakfast, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Hotel Ritz Lisbon
voyage.content: Five-star, 282-room hotel with spa, gym, swimming pool, restaurant, and bar. The decor is a mix of Art Deco and Louis XVI, with a collection of mid-20th-century Portuguese art.

voyage.name: HI Lisboa – Pousada de Juventude
voyage.content: 32-room youth hostel with free breakfast and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Intercontinental Lisbon Hotel
voyage.content: Five-star, 331-room hotel overlooking Parque Eduardo VII. Amenities include fitness centre, bar, business centre, conference facilities, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Lisbon Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: Four-star, 577-room hotel with swimming pool, gym, bar, conference facilities, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Novotel Lisboa
voyage.content: Four-star, 249-room hotel with swimming pool, gym, bar, and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Sheraton Lisboa Hotel & Spa
voyage.content: Five-star, 369-room hotel with swimming pool, spa, gym, business centre, and free Wi-Fi. Its rooftop Panorama Restaurant and Bar offers superb views over Lisbon.
